name: ziplark-mcp
description: Read, preview, extract, add & create archives — ZIP, RAR, 7z, tar, ISO, DEB, RPM, CAB, CPIO, AR — from an MCP client.
long_description: Ziplark's archive engine over the Model Context Protocol. Lists, reads/previews in memory, extracts (including smart anti-tarbomb extraction), verifies, appends to, and creates archives: ZIP (incl. .z01/.zip.001 split, .crx, .jar, .apk, .whl), RAR and RAR5 (including multi-volume sets, encrypted headers and self-extracting archives), 7z (incl. .7z.001 multi-volume), tar and the compressed-tar variants, single-stream gz/bz2/xz/zst/lz4, ISO 9660 / Joliet disc images, Debian (.deb) & Unix ar (.ar, .a), Red Hat (.rpm) & CPIO (.cpio.*), and Microsoft Cabinet (.cab). Listings and in-memory file reads are paged so huge archives never flood the context, and every extraction path is funnelled through a single guard so no entry can escape the destination directory. Read tools (ziplark_info, ziplark_list, ziplark_read, ziplark_test) are always available; extracting, creating and appending require --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_info
tools.description: What kind of archive this is and what shape it is in: format, entry count, sizes, encryption, and — for a multi-volume set — its volumes, whether one is missing, whether it is solid, and its comment.

tools.name: ziplark_list
tools.description: List the entries inside an archive, paged, with per-directory counts when the result is truncated.

tools.name: ziplark_read
tools.description: Read a single entry inside an archive into memory without extracting anything to disk, with offset and max_bytes paging.

tools.name: ziplark_test
tools.description: Verify archive integrity by decompressing every entry. Writes nothing, and reports every bad entry rather than the first.

tools.name: ziplark_extract
tools.description: Extract an archive, or exactly the entries named, into a destination directory (with optional smart anti-tarbomb mode). Requires --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_create
tools.description: Create a ZIP (AES-256), 7z (AES-256) or tar archive from files and directories. Requires --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_add
tools.description: Add or replace files/directories inside an existing archive (zip, 7z, tar.*), or create it if it does not exist. Requires --allow-write.
